_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: Drift Wood #7 · the caricature
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 17, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; GULLY — aged 18, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Gully draws Mr. Hadley as a walrus. Mr. Hadley confiscates it. Then keeps it. Panel 1: a high school journalism classroom, a mustached teacher in a sweater vest at a chalkboard, two boys in the back row, one drawing on scrap paper (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). Mr. Hadley says "The inverted pyramid puts the most important information first—". Panel 2: close-up of a ballpoint caricature on scrap paper of a mustached teacher drawn as a walrus in a sweater vest holding chalk, surprisingly skilled. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a teacher standing over a desk holding a confiscated drawing and looking at it with an unreadable expression, a boy in a backwards cap braced (in this panel: GULLY). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: a teacher back at the chalkboard with a folded paper in his sweater-vest pocket, two boys in the back row whispering (in this panel: WOOD, GULLY). Mr. Hadley says "—the least important information last.". Wood says "He kept it.". Gully says "They always keep it.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
